title: Pilot weekly eval — model switchback strategy & pinning

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-07 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Chen (Redwood SE), Amina Torres (Sirius - AI/ML Lead), Benji Cole (Sirius - CTO), Priya Nair (Sirius - Security)
Links referenced: deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/pilot-deck), benchmark sheet (internal link: redwood://benchmarks/sirius-poc), security packet (sent earlier: link omitted)

Summary: Quick walk-through of the latest model run outputs, explainers on why the v2-small quantized variant regressed on hallucination set, proposal for an automated switchback window and a pinned model hierarchy. Short demo of the rollback script.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Alri- good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 54 minutes on the calendar. I'll run quick intro, Samira's going to run through the evaluation table, then we'll discuss pinning rules and rollback. Does that sound good?
[00:18] Amina: Yeah that works, thanks Jordan. Quick note, Benji had a calendar conflict so he may drop and rejoin.
[00:28] Samira: Great, I'm sharing my screen — okay, can you see the benchmark sheet? I'm on the 'variant outputs' tab.
[00:35] Amina: Yep I can see it. It's a lot of rows, thanks.
[00:40] Samira: So top summary — latency median's within SLO for all variants except the quantized v2-small under 512 tokens, where tail spikes to about 420ms at the 95th. The bigger issue though is hallucination score, we ran the labeled prompts and v2-small has a +8% hallucination delta versus baseline v1-bertlike.
[01:02] Priya: Sorry, when you say hallucination delta, remind me how that was computed? Is that exact-match on entity extraction or a manual label?
[01:10] Samira: It's a mix — we used the customer-provided hallucination rubric Amina sent plus an automated scorer for entity hallucination. There's still some noise, that's why I'm flagging manual review for the top 20 failures.
[01:24] Jordan: Important for decisioning — is the hallucination pattern systematic (e.g., with certain prompt templates) or more random?
[01:31] Samira: Mostly with multi-turn clinical summarization prompts where the models invent patient meds when not present. We looked at the prompt tags; the prompts with 'summary-with-history' tag show highest delta.
[01:46] Amina: Hmm, ok. Our acceptance criteria was 2% max hallucination rate, so +8% is out of bounds.
[01:54] Benji (rejoining): Hey, sorry I'm back. Did I miss anything big?
[01:59] Jordan: quick recap: quantized v2-small shows latency tail and hallucination regression on the clinical summary suite. We're discussing pin/switchback strategy.
[02:08] Benji: Got it. My priority is keeping the P95 latency under 380ms and no regressions on that hallucination rubric.
[02:17] Samira: Proposed approach: 1) For host: pin production traffic to v1-stable by default; 2) allow experimental routed traffic to v2-small at a 5% canary; 3) if hallucination delta >4% or P95 >400ms, auto-switchback to last stable within 10 minutes and alert on Slack + PagerDuty.
[02:40] Priya: From security/compliance side, we need audit logs of any automated switchback and the model IDs involved. Also need to ensure KMS keys for the private pilot are not rotated mid-test.
[02:53] Jordan: Absolutely, we can wire the audit entries into your SIEM and include model version and full hash in the event.
[02:59] Amina: Quick question — if we auto-switchback, will the user-facing session preserve KV cache or will we start fresh? For our multi-turn tests preserving context is important.
[03:12] Samira: Good call — currently our switchback plan invalidates the KV cache for safety, but we can offer a 'soft switchback' that routes new requests to fallback while continuing the old instance for existing sessions for up to 2 minutes. There's a trade-off between safety and continuity.
[03:29] Benji: Soft sounds good for UX, but we need a way to force immediate rollback for safety incidents.
[03:36] Jordan: We'll expose both: an automatic policy with soft switchback by default and a manual forced rollback button that the customer can press (requires two SSO confirmations per your security policy).
[03:47] Samira: For rollbacks we also have a 'burn-in' check — an automated suite that runs 50 synthetic prompts against the candidate rollback variant before it goes live. That can be toggled in the deployment config.
[03:59] Amina: How long does the burn-in take?
[04:03] Samira: Typically under 90 seconds for the smoke set, but for your full hallucination suite it's more like 6–8 minutes.
[04:12] Priya: We want the burn-in to record a signed artifact showing the hash of the model and the checksum of the prompt set for audit. Is that available?
[04:21] Samira: Yes, we can produce a signed artifact and push it to your S3 or to your internal artifact store. We'll include the exact commit and quantization parameters.
[04:33] Jordan: Ok moving on — open question: do you want to pin at the model family level (e.g., v1 vs v2) or exact model digest (v1-2025-09-01-digest)? Pinning to digest gives maximum determinism but loses ability to get minor non-breaking fixes.
[04:50] Benji: I think digest pinning for production endpoints, family pinning for canaries. We want to avoid silent drift in prod.
[04:58] Amina: Agreed. Also we want an explicit rollover window for upgrades: a canary period of 24–48 hours with increased monitoring.
[05:08] Samira: We'll add a 'canary window' config parameter to the route, default 24 hours, and a 'rollover backoff' for forced retries.
[05:17] Jordan: Let's talk rollback script demo — Samira over to you.
[05:22] Samira: I'm demoing a small script that hits the Redwood API to create a new route with a pinned digest and a fallback sequence. Running it now (typing noises)...
[05:35] Samira: Done — the script returned an operation ID. If we poll the operation you'll see steps: create route -> deploy -> run burn-in -> promote.
[05:44] Amina: Can that script be used by our CICD? We want to integrate with our deploy pipeline.
[05:49] Samira: Yes it can; we have a CLI and a REST call. We can add an example GitHub Actions workflow.
[05:55] Benji: If we integrate, can we also attach release notes that get stored with the audit entry?
[06:03] Jordan: Absolutely, the endpoint accepts a metadata field 'release_notes' and we'll store it with the operation audit.
[06:10] Priya: On encryption — we're good with envelope encryption but need to validate the KMS rotations schedule. We'll send the policy.
[06:17] Amina: Back to the hallucination issue: do you think quantization caused it or is it a model architecture difference?
[06:25] Samira: Preliminary signal points to quantization artifacts in the head-layer attention causing token probabilities to slightly shift—this combined with the concise clinical prompts amplifies incorrect token sampling. We need more A/Bs.
[06:40] Benji: Could we try a mixed configuration: run v2-small quantized for non-summary prompts and use v1 for 'summary-with-history' tagged prompts? Route by tag?
[06:50] Samira: Yes, we support attribute-based routing — you can route by prompt tag, user segment, or request size. That would limit exposure to the failing prompt family.
[07:01] Amina: Nice. Ok, action items?
[07:05] Jordan: I'll capture those. Meanwhile, any blockers from security?
[07:09] Priya: Need to verify the signed artifact flow and whether we can ingest the audit JSON into our SIEM. Also confirm RBAC so only two named users can trigger forced rollback.
[07:21] Jordan: We'll send an architecture note on RBAC and the webhook format.
[07:26] Samira: Quick note — we observed a small memory leak in one of our early dedicated instances on the private pilot; it's not in hosted but we'll patch and push a build. Shouldn't affect you unless you use dedicated pools.
[07:42] Benji: We're on hosted for now but planned dedicated later in Q1. Keep me posted on that patch.
[07:49] Jordan: Sure.
[07:52] Samira: I'll run one more table — here's a proposed pinned matrix: production endpoints = v1-digest-2025-09-01, canary routes = v2-small-quant-2025-10-02 at 5%, fallback sequence = [v1-digest-2025-09-01, v1-digest-2025-08-15].
[08:14] Amina: Looks reasonable. Can you also include soft switchback settings and the KV cache preservation option?
[08:22] Samira: Yes, add 'soft_switchback:true' and 'preserve_sessions_window:120s' to the config.
[08:28] Benji: What about alerting thresholds? We want an obvious tripwire at +3% hallucination or P95 >380ms.
[08:36] Jordan: We can make those thresholds configurable per-route. We'll set defaults to your suggested values for the pilot.
[08:44] Amina: One last perf ask — can we capture per-token time for the first 50 tokens so we can diagnose the warm vs KV-cache cost?
[08:53] Samira: Yep we provide per-token timing in the tracing hook; we'll enable sampling at 10% for now.
[09:02] Jordan: Ok, let's set concrete next-steps and owners: Jordan will send the pinned model matrix and recommended test plan, Samira will push the rollback scripts and example CI workflow, Amina will share the hallucination prompt subset. Priya will confirm KMS constraints. Any objections?
[09:23] Amina: No objections.
[09:24] Benji: Sounds good.
[09:26] Priya: All right.
[09:28] Jordan: Anything else? If not we'll wrap. Thanks everyone.
[09:32] Samira: One quick thing — we're scheduling a 95th-percentile performance run next Wednesday at 2pm. Want to join?
[09:39] Benji: Yes, I'll join.
[09:41] Amina: I'll try to.
[09:44] Jordan: Great, we'll send calendar invite. Wrap up in next steps.

End transcript.
